subject: Dedicated capacity sizing — memory & quantization risk analysis for POC
messages:
From: Sarah Wu <sarah.wu@orchidtx.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 8 Mar 2028 09:21:00 -0800
Subject: Sizing request — dedicated capacity for Chem-POC

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the chat yesterday. As discussed, we're lining up a 6‑week POC to run our chemistry-informatics generator against our internal design-of-experiments workload. We have two primary concerns: (1) long-context sessions (up to ~40k tokens) while preserving KV cache for interactive flows, and (2) whether quantization will materially change how many GPUs we must reserve.

Quick background: typical session length ~ 8–10k tokens, but we have exploratory runs up to 40k. Expected concurrency during peak: 12 simultaneous sessions (mostly interactive), expected 95th latency SLO ~ 400ms per token for interactive mode.

Can you send a short analysis of model-specific memory footprints (model weights + KV cache) for the variants we discussed and a recommendation for a reserved GPU footprint to cover peak with a sensible safety margin? Also attaching a small sample trace and one representative long session so you can see token/turn distributions.

Attachments: sample-session-traces.tar.gz (3 files: short_sessions.jsonl, long_session_40k.jsonl, aggregate_token_hist.csv)

Appreciate a concise runbook we can hand to procurement.

Cheers,
Sarah Wu
Head of ML Engineering
Orchid Therapeutics

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Wu <sarah.wu@orchidtx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing request — dedicated capacity for Chem-POC

Sarah — thanks for the traces and the context. Looping in Marissa (SE) and Priyom (AE) to align on sizing and procurement cadence. Below is a short, model-centric memory breakdown and our initial recommendation. We can convert this into a one‑page mutual action plan for procurement.

Key assumptions:
- Model candidates: Redwood-v3-13B (RV3-13B), Open-LLM-70B-chat (OL-70B-chat).
- Runtime: BF16/FP16 by default on A100/H100; quantized runs tested on int8 (QAT) and 4-bit variants (Q4_0).
- KV cache scales linearly with context length and is stored per‑token per‑layer activation (approx).

Initial memory estimates (per GPU worker, single copy):
- RV3-13B (FP16): model weights ~ 13 GB, activations/KV for 40k context (single session) ~ 20–22 GB; working set ~ 35 GB.
- RV3-13B (int8/Q4): model weights compress to ~3.5–5 GB depending on quant scheme; KV cache unaffected (~20–22 GB). Working set still ~24–28 GB.
- OL-70B-chat (FP16): weights ~ 35–40 GB, KV 40k context ~ 35–40 GB; working set ~75–80 GB (rare for single GPU).
- OL-70B-chat (8-bit): weights ~11–14 GB; KV still large, working set ~46–54 GB.

Takeaways: 1) Quantization drastically reduces model weight residency but does NOT materially reduce KV cache; for long-context workloads KV dominates. 2) For interactive, high-concurrency scenarios, we recommend prioritizing more GPU workers sized for KV (i.e., memory capacity per worker) rather than only relying on quantization to reduce instance count.

Recommended dedicated pool for initial POC (to cover 12 concurrent sessions during peak, 40k worst-case, 95% safety margin):
- Option A (lower-cost): RV3-13B quantized(8-bit) pinned to 48 GB GPU instances (H100-48) — 4 workers (scale to 6 if burst > 12) — estimated steady RBW: 4 x 48GB = 192GB total; reserve: 4 workers.
- Option B (higher-headroom): RV3-13B FP16 on 80GB-class GPUs (H100-80) — 3 workers, gives headroom for mixed workloads and easier scheduling.

Operational mitigations we recommend:
- Prefix and KV caching at the service layer for repeated prefixes.
- KV offload to CPU for long tail (trade latency for capacity) as a controlled fallback.
- Model fallbacks (RV3-13B -> RV3-7B) configured in routing policy for overload.

Pending items for more accurate sizing:
- Expected ratio of long (~40k) vs short sessions during peak (we used conservative 20% long).
- Tokens/sec/prompt for interactive flows (to estimate GPU utilization and batching).

I'll produce a short spreadsheet with per‑worker RAM math and a recommended procurement note. Marissa — can you add the per‑layer KV estimates we use in bench runs and any microbench numbers?

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0187

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Sarah Wu <sarah.wu@orchidtx.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing request — dedicated capacity for Chem-POC

Thanks Rafael — adding the microbench details and a short table. Quick note: our microbench KV numbers are conservative and assume no prefix sharing. If Orchid can accept prefix cache on the RDW side for repeated molecule scaffolds, effective KV can drop dramatically for interactive flows.

Microbench-derived numbers (approx):
- RV3-13B: KV per token ~ 0.00055 GB (per-token per-session aggregate across layers).
  - 10k tokens -> ~5.5 GB KV; 40k tokens -> ~22 GB KV.
- OL-70B-chat: KV per token ~ 0.0009 GB -> 40k tokens ~36 GB KV.

Model weight residency (examples):
- RV3-13B FP16: 12.8 GB
- RV3-13B Q4_0: 4.1 GB
- RV3-13B Q8: 3.6 GB

Practical per-GPU working-set scenarios (single long session pinned on a worker):
- RV3-13B Q8 on 48GB GPU: model(3.6GB) + KV40k(22GB) + runtime buffers/batch ~ 6–8GB => fits in ~32–34GB, leaving ~14–16GB for extra sessions or batching.
- RV3-13B FP16 on 80GB GPU: ample headroom for 2 simultaneous long sessions when batching is enabled.

Notes on quantization impact:
- Gains: less pinned model RAM, faster cold-starts for model load, smaller checkpoint footprint.
- Limits: KV cache is the dominant term for long contexts and does not compress with weight quantization. Also quantization adds micro-variance to perf; we recommend validating prompt fidelity for chemistry-critical scoring before committing.

Attached: orchid_capacity_calculator.xlsx — small sheet with per-session math and a PoC reserve recommendation. Rafael / Priyom — I'll prepare a one-page procurement note with SKU recommendations and minimal SLA text.

-marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Wu <sarah.wu@orchidtx.com>

Subject: Re: Sizing request — dedicated capacity for Chem-POC

This is excellent — thanks all. The numbers align with what our infra team sketched. A couple of quick follow-ups:

1) For the POC we prefer Option A (quantized RV3-13B on 48GB workers). Please prepare a short procurement note and a contract addendum (1 month reserved capacity + auto-burst) we can use to expedite review.

2) Can you confirm fallback routing behavior if KV-offload is triggered? We need a short sentence for our security/compliance team outlining whether any token-level data crosses customer VPC boundaries during offload.

3) We're likely to ask for a small one‑time POC credit (3–4k USD) given the exploratory long-context burden. Priyom — would you own the credit request?

Next steps: Rafael — if you can drop the procurement note + proposed PSA this week, we'll start procurement and routing review. I'll attach procurement contacts in the follow-up.
